title: 5 things to know about Kim You-jung, the star of “100 Days of Deception” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao November 9, 2026 Having spent more than two decades in the entertainment industry, Kim You-jung is no stranger to the spotlight. Now, she's capturing audiences' attention once again with "100 Days of Deception," the historical spy romance that's been climbing the K-drama ratings. Set during the Japanese occupation of Korea, the series follows Lee Ga-gyeong (Kim You-jung), a skilled pickpocket who goes undercover for the independence movement and crosses paths with an elite interpreter played by Park Jinyoung. But how much do you know about the actress behind the character? Here are five things worth knowing 
 She made her debut at just four years old
 Photo: Instagram @you_r_love
 While most four-year-olds were busy playing, Kim You-jung was already stepping in front of the camera. Born in 1999, she began her career in a commercial for Crown Sando biscuits in 2003 before making her film debut in Demilitarized Zone the following year. She soon became one of South Korea's most recognisable child actresses, frequently playing younger versions of leading characters. In fact, she once revealed that she started acting so young that studying her scripts even helped her learn to read Korean.
 She's known as the “Nation's Little Sister” and “Sageuk Fairy”
 Photo: Netflix
 Over the years, Kim You-jung has earned not one, but two affectionate nicknames. Her popularity as a child actress earned her the title "Nation's Little Sister", while her performances in historical dramas like Moon Embracing the Sun made her known as the "Sageuk Fairy". Her biggest breakthrough came with the 2016 hit Love in the Moonlight, where she played a young woman disguised as a palace eunuch who falls in love with a crown prince played by Park Bo-gum. Just 16 when filming began, Kim's performance helped establish her as a leading actress beyond her child-star days.

 She spent five months studying Japanese for her latest role
 Photo: Instagram @you_r_love
 Kim You-jung certainly put in the work for 100 Days of Deception . To portray Lee Ga-gyeong, who uses Japanese and English while working undercover, the actress spent around five months studying Japanese before filming. She reportedly attended nearly two lessons a day, covering everything from grammar and conversation to practising her lines. She also paid close attention to her English delivery, making sure it sounded like someone who had picked up the language by listening to others rather than through formal lessons. It's the kind of detail that shows just how seriously she takes her roles.
 She has a creative side beyond acting
 Photo: Instagram @you_r_love
 Acting isn't Kim You-jung's only creative outlet. When she's not busy filming, she enjoys painting, particularly with oils and acrylics. Her interest in painting actually began by chance when she tried a drawing class while studying photography, and she's been hooked ever since. She particularly enjoys creating abstract works inspired by emotions, music and scenes that come to mind. Interestingly, she also believes painting has helped her become a better actress, giving her another way to explore and express emotions beyond scripts and dialogue.
 She became ChildFund Korea's youngest major donor
 Photo: Instagram @you_r_love
 Beyond the screen, Kim You-jung has also made headlines for her generosity. In October 2020, at just 21 years old, she became the youngest member at the time of ChildFund Korea's Green Noble Club, which recognises people who have donated at least KRW 100 million. What's even more touching is that she had been making donations quietly through an intermediary rather than under her own name. Her contributions have helped children from low-income families affected by COVID-19, while also providing financial support for young patients in need of medical treatment.
